policies.purpose: To set uniform admission criteria and a pre-acceptance assessment process so that [AGENCY NAME] accepts only clients whose needs it can safely meet, verifies Medicaid eligibility, and gives every client the required information before services begin.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] accepts a client only after intake screening and a pre-acceptance assessment confirm that the agency can safely meet the client's needs within its Scope of Services (SVC-01) and with available qualified staff. An assessment is completed before services begin. The only exceptions are limited cases in which no skilled care has been requested and there is no reason to believe skilled care is needed. For CFC, the participant must have institutional level of care, Medicaid eligibility and a home residence, and the plan of service must name [AGENCY NAME] as the participant's chosen personal assistance agency. The agency verifies Medicaid eligibility at the start of each month of service. At intake, the agency records any client representative and advance directive information and gives the client the required information packet.

definitions.definition: The written conditions a prospective client must meet for the agency to accept them: needs within the Scope of Services, a safe home environment, available qualified staff, and, for Medicaid, eligibility and an authorized plan of service.
The screening and assessment of a prospective client's needs, home and supports before the agency agrees to provide services.
The level of care determination required for CFC participation, confirmed through the Medicaid program.
The Medicaid document prepared by the supports planner or case manager that authorizes services and names the personal assistance agency the participant chooses.

procedures: The Intake Coordinator records each referral or request on the Intake Form, including the date and time of the request, who made it, the client's contact information, payer source, and any request for skilled care. A request for services starts the assessment timelines in SVC-03.

The Intake Coordinator screens the request against the written admission criteria and the Scope of Services Schedule. If the request is clearly outside the scope (for example, a skilled service the agency does not offer), the Coordinator tells the caller the same day, offers to help find another provider, and documents the referral.

For Medicaid referrals, the Intake Coordinator confirms that the plan of service from the supports planner or case manager names [AGENCY NAME], lists the authorized services and hours, and shows the participant lives at home. The Coordinator confirms institutional level of care through the plan of service or with the supports planner.

The Intake Coordinator verifies Medicaid eligibility in the State's eligibility verification system before the first visit and at the start of every month of service. The result (date, staff initials) is filed in the client record. If eligibility cannot be confirmed, the Coordinator tells the Administrator and the supports planner before services are provided or continued (SVC-09).

The Supervising RN is notified of every new referral within one business day and decides if the pre-acceptance assessment can be done by phone or must be done in the home. The Supervising RN conducts the assessment for any client requesting or likely to need skilled services, or any new CFC/CPAS participant.

The pre-acceptance assessment covers health conditions, functional ability (ADLs and IADLs), cognition and communication, medications, home safety, available informal supports, special equipment, and the client's goals and preferences. The Supervising RN documents it on the Pre-Acceptance Assessment Form.

If the client requests skilled care or the RN has reason to believe skilled care is needed, the RN assessment is completed before services begin. If the client has asked for no skilled care and there is no reason to believe it is needed, services may begin after the intake screening, and the RN completes the plan of care assessment under SVC-03.

The Supervising RN and Administrator decide on acceptance. The decision and reasons are documented. If the agency declines, the Intake Coordinator tells the client or representative in writing and offers other resources, including the supports planner or case manager for Medicaid clients.

At intake, the Intake Coordinator asks whether the client has a guardian, advance directive, surrogate decision maker, power of attorney, representative payee or a person designated in writing, and files a copy of the authorizing document or records the representative's name (CR-08). The agency does not honor a representative who exceeds the authority granted.

Before or at the first visit, the Intake Coordinator or Supervising RN provides the client or representative with the information packet: client rights and responsibilities (CR-01), grievance procedure (CR-02), privacy notice (CR-03), written cost estimate and rates (CR-06), the name of the assigned caregiver, the Supervising RN's name and contact information, the 24/7 phone number, and the written on-call procedures (SVC-11).

The client or representative signs the Service Agreement and an acknowledgment that the packet was received. Copies are given to the client and filed in the record. If informed consent or a waiver of skilled services is required, the process in CR-07 is completed before the related services start.

The Intake Coordinator confirms with the Medicaid participant that the participant chose [AGENCY NAME] and explains participant direction (CR-09), including the participant's right to select, train, schedule and dismiss a worker.
The Scheduler confirms a qualified caregiver is available (SVC-05) before the start date. The participant's representative may not be assigned as the participant's worker.
The Intake Coordinator forwards the completed intake packet to the Supervising RN, who completes the plan of care assessment (SVC-03) and files everything in the clinical record (REC-01).
The Administrator reviews intake logs monthly for timeliness, declined referrals and eligibility verification, and reports the results to the QA program (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Takes referrals, screens against the admission criteria, verifies Medicaid eligibility, collects representative information, and delivers the information packet.
Performs pre-acceptance and plan of care assessments, decides whether skilled needs can be met, and takes part in acceptance decisions.
Makes final acceptance decisions, ensures admission criteria are followed, and reviews intake performance.
Confirms a qualified caregiver is available before services start.

documentation: Intake Form showing the date and time of the request
Pre-Acceptance Assessment Form
Monthly Medicaid eligibility verification record
Plan of service naming the agency
Representative documents or the representative's name
Signed Service Agreement and packet receipt
Notice of non-acceptance, if applicable

policies.title: RN Assessment, Plan of Care / Plan of Service and Plan Updates
policies.applies_to: Supervising RN, schedulers, caregivers; all clients and CFC/CPAS participants
policies.purpose: To ensure each client receives a timely RN assessment and a written plan of care or plan of service that is based on assessed need, matches Medicaid authorizations, and is updated when the client's condition changes.
policies.policy: A registered nurse (RN) employed by [AGENCY NAME] assesses each new client who requires skilled services and ADL help, and each new CFC/CPAS participant who needs personal assistance. The RN helps develop the plan of care and worker instructions, helps assign staff, and decides whether a CNA is needed. The plan of care is based on assessment of the client's health, function and psychosocial condition. It states the services to be provided, when and how often, how and by whom, long- and short-range goals, and safety measures. The RN reassesses at least annually, on request of the client or representative, and within 48 hours of a listed skilled need or a significant change in condition (or within 7 calendar days if the RN documents in the record why the 48-hour assessment is unnecessary). The agency applies the timing exceptions the regulation allows for weather emergencies, natural disasters and declared emergencies, and documents them. Scheduled hours must match the Medicaid plan of service and must never exceed authorized hours.

definitions.definition: The RN-developed written plan for each client stating services, frequency, who provides them and how, goals and safety measures.
The Medicaid plan prepared by the supports planner or case manager that authorizes the type and amount of services for a CFC/CPAS participant.
A change in the client's health, function, cognition or safety that may require a change in services, such as a fall, hospitalization, new skilled need or decline in ability.
The limit on Medicaid services based on the participant's assessed need.

procedures: When a request for services is received, the Intake Coordinator notifies the Supervising RN the same business day (SVC-02) and records the date of the request. The RN assessment timelines run from that date.

The Supervising RN performs the initial assessment in the client's home before services start, except in the limited cases allowed in SVC-02. The RN reviews the plan of service, medical information, medication list, physician orders if any, and the client's own goals.

The RN documents the assessment of health status, ADLs and IADLs, mobility and fall risk, skin, nutrition, cognition, mood, medications, communication, equipment, home safety, caregiver and family supports, and psychosocial condition, using the agency's Assessment Form.

The RN develops the plan of care (or worker instructions for a Medicaid participant) with the client or representative. It states each service, when and how often it is provided, how and by whom, long- and short-range goals, and safety measures. The RN uses the OLTSS Standardized Times SOP to plan task times.

For Medicaid participants, the RN compares the plan of care to the plan of service and confirms the hours scheduled do not exceed the authorized hours or the service budget. If the assessed need exceeds the authorized hours, the RN notifies the supports planner or case manager (SVC-13) and the agency does not provide or bill hours that are not authorized.
The RN decides whether a CNA or CMT is needed or whether a non-certified aide may be assigned, and records the determination in the record (SVC-05).

The client or representative reviews the plan of care and signs and dates it. The RN gives a copy to the client or representative and the Scheduler receives the task instructions. If the client declines part of the plan, the RN discusses the risks and benefits, documents the discussion, and uses CR-07 when a waiver or informed consent is needed.

The RN trains or instructs each assigned caregiver on the plan before the caregiver's first visit and documents it (SVC-04). Caregivers receive the task instructions at the client's home or by secure means, and the client's copy is kept in the home.

The RN reassesses within 48 hours when the client has a listed skilled need or a significant change in condition. If the RN decides a 48-hour assessment is unnecessary, the RN documents the reason in the record and completes the assessment within 7 calendar days.

During a weather emergency, natural disaster or declared emergency, the RN may use the timing exceptions allowed by the regulation. The RN documents the emergency, the reason the assessment could not be done on time, the interim steps taken to protect the client, and the date the assessment was completed.
The RN reassesses at least annually, no later than 12 months from the last assessment. The Scheduler and RN use a tracking log that flags upcoming due dates 30 days ahead.

The RN reassesses on the request of the client or representative. Any staff member who receives such a request tells the RN the same business day, and the RN sets a visit within a timeframe suited to the client's condition.

After each reassessment, the RN updates the plan of care, tells the caregivers, tells the Scheduler of changes in tasks or hours, and notifies the supports planner or case manager of any Medicaid-related change. Changes in services or hours for a Medicaid participant take effect only with Department authorization.

Caregivers report changes in condition to the Supervising RN the same day (SVC-10). The RN reviews the report, decides if an assessment is needed within the required timeframe, and documents the decision.
The Administrator reviews the tracking log monthly for overdue assessments and plan updates and reports the results to the QA program (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Performs all required assessments, develops and updates the plan of care, determines CNA need, and documents timing exceptions.
Records the date of request and notifies the RN the same business day.
Schedules only authorized hours consistent with the plan and keeps the reassessment tracking log.
Follows the plan of care and task instructions and reports changes in condition the same day.
Monitors timeliness and corrects delays.

documentation: Date and time of the request for services
Completed RN Assessment Forms for initial, 48-hour or 7-day, request-based and annual assessments
Plan of care with the client or representative's signature and date
Documented reason when the assessment is done within 7 calendar days instead of 48 hours
Documentation of emergency timing exceptions
Comparison of scheduled hours to the plan of service
Reassessment tracking log

policies.title: Nursing Oversight, Delegation and Supervisory Visits
policies.applies_to: Supervising RN, CNAs, CMTs, non-certified aides, Administrator, schedulers
policies.purpose: To ensure that a registered nurse oversees care-plan implementation, delegates nursing tasks only as allowed, supervises caregivers in the client's home at required intervals, and coordinates with the participant's nurse monitor.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] employs a registered nurse (RN) who oversees implementation of each plan of care, delegates nursing tasks, supervises caregivers and helps train staff. Under CFC and CPAS, the RN delegates nursing tasks only to a CNA or CMT under COMAR 10.27.11 and instructs workers. The RN performs on-site supervision of the caregiver in the client's home at least every 45 days when staff administer medications, at least every 3 months when staff assist with self-administration, and at least every 4 months when neither applies. The RN may set a shorter interval based on the client's condition. Each supervisory visit is documented accurately. For Medicaid participants, the agency coordinates with the participant's nurse monitor, who has contact every 6 months and an in-person visit every 12 months, and agency staff cooperate fully with the nurse monitor.

definitions.definition: The RN's transfer of a specific nursing task for a specific client to a qualified CNA or CMT, with instruction and ongoing supervision, under COMAR 10.27.11.
An on-site visit by the RN to the client's home to observe the caregiver, evaluate the client's condition and review the plan of care.
A nurse monitoring provider designated by the Department who contacts and visits the participant to monitor services; separate from the agency's own RN.
Certified Medication Technician, who may administer medications under delegation.

procedures: The Supervising RN determines the supervisory visit interval for each client at the initial assessment: every 45 days if staff administer medications, every 3 months if staff assist with self-administration, and every 4 months otherwise. The RN may set a shorter interval based on the client's condition and writes the interval and reason in the plan of care.

Before delegating any nursing task, the RN confirms that the caregiver holds the required credential (CNA for delegated nursing tasks, CMT for medication administration), that the task is within the Scope of Services (SVC-01), and that the client's condition is stable enough for delegation.

The RN delegates each task for each client in writing on the Delegation Form, naming the caregiver, the task, the client, the instructions, and the circumstances in which the caregiver must call the RN. The RN instructs and demonstrates the task and checks the caregiver's understanding. The RN and the caregiver both sign and date the form.
The RN does not delegate tasks that require nursing judgment or assessment, or tasks outside the caregiver's credential, and tells the caregiver and Scheduler which tasks are not delegated.

The RN gives the caregiver written task instructions before the first visit and instructs the caregiver on any change in the plan. The RN also accepts instruction on the plan of service from the participant or representative, the nurse monitor, a treating physician or nurse practitioner, or MDH, and incorporates it in the worker instructions.

The Scheduler maintains a Supervisory Visit Calendar showing the next due date for each client and notifies the RN 14 days before each due date. The RN schedules the visit with the client and caregiver.

At each supervisory visit, the RN observes the caregiver giving care, evaluates the client's condition and satisfaction, reviews the plan of care and delegation, checks the medication record and any errors, reviews home safety and infection control, and confirms the caregiver's time records match the plan.

The RN documents each visit the same day on the Supervisory Visit Form: date, time, who was present, findings, instruction given, changes made to the plan, and follow-up. The RN signs and dates it and files it in the clinical record.

If a visit finds the caregiver cannot perform a task safely, the RN stops the delegation immediately, retrains the caregiver or arranges a different caregiver, informs the Scheduler, and documents the action. Conduct that may be grounds for Board of Nursing action is reported under PER-10.
If a visit finds a significant change in the client's condition, the RN completes a reassessment within the timeframe in SVC-03 and updates the plan of care.

If a supervisory visit cannot be done by the due date (for example, because the client is hospitalized or refuses entry), the RN documents the reason, reschedules at the earliest safe date, and tells the Administrator. A missed interval is never left undocumented.

For Medicaid participants, the RN coordinates with the participant's nurse monitor. The RN shares requested information and cooperates with the nurse monitor's contacts (every 6 months) and in-person visits (every 12 months), and asks the nurse monitor for any plan-of-service changes it recommends. The RN documents each contact in the record.

Caregivers cooperate with supervisory visits and the nurse monitor, follow the RN's instructions, and call the RN or the on-call number (SVC-11) when a client's condition or a task is outside the instructions.
The Administrator reviews the Supervisory Visit Calendar monthly for overdue visits and reports to the QA program (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Sets visit intervals, delegates and instructs, conducts and documents supervisory visits, and coordinates with the nurse monitor.
Maintains the Supervisory Visit Calendar and gives the RN advance reminders.
Performs only delegated tasks as instructed and reports concerns to the RN.
Ensures the agency employs an RN with sufficient time to supervise and reviews timeliness of visits.

documentation: Supervisory visit interval and reason in the plan of care
Signed Delegation Forms
Supervisory Visit Forms
Supervisory Visit Calendar
Documented reasons for any late visit
Records of nurse monitor contacts and information shared
RN license verification (PER-01)

policies.title: Assigning Certified Caregivers (CNA/CMT) and Non-Certified Aides
policies.applies_to: Supervising RN, Scheduler, Administrator, caregivers
policies.purpose: To make sure each client is assigned a caregiver with the credential the client's needs require, and that non-certified aides are assigned only in the situations the regulation allows.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] assigns a certified caregiver (CNA, or CMT for medication administration) to every client who needs a certified caregiver for ADLs or who needs medication administered. A non-certified caregiver may be assigned only if (1) the client needs no ADL help, (2) the client needs ADL help with no predictable adverse health consequences in the supervising nurse's judgment, or (3) the client signs a waiver of skilled services after the informed consent process. The Supervising RN makes and documents the determination of whether the client needs a CNA. Under CFC, a worker who administers medication under the plan of service must be a CMT, and a worker who performs other delegated nursing functions must also be a CNA. The participant's representative is never assigned as the participant's worker.

definitions.definition: A caregiver who holds current Maryland certification, such as CNA or CMT, verified under PER-01.
A caregiver who has completed the agency's screening, orientation and skills assessment but holds no CNA or CMT certification.
A signed and dated form by which a client, after a documented risk and benefit discussion, accepts a non-certified caregiver for ADL help.
A foreseeable harm to the client's health that could result if ADL help is given by someone without certification, as judged by the supervising nurse.

procedures: At the initial assessment and each reassessment, the Supervising RN decides whether the client needs a certified caregiver, using the client's ADL needs, medication needs, diagnoses, risk factors and stability. The RN records the determination, the reasoning and the date on the Caregiver Qualification Determination in the client record.

The RN selects one of four outcomes: (a) CNA required for ADLs; (b) CMT required for medication administration; (c) non-certified aide allowed because the client needs no ADL help or the RN judges there are no predictable adverse health consequences; or (d) non-certified aide allowed under a signed waiver of skilled services.
For outcome (c), the RN documents the specific clinical judgment about why ADL help carries no predictable adverse health consequences, and reviews it at every supervisory visit and reassessment.

For outcome (d), the RN completes the informed consent and waiver process under CR-07: a documented discussion of risks and benefits, signature and date by the client or authorized representative, and a copy given to the client and filed in the record. The agency does not assign a non-certified aide for ADL help before the waiver is signed.
The RN gives the Scheduler a written staffing requirement for each client (for example, 'CNA required' or 'CMT required for medication administration'), which is recorded in the scheduling system.

Before each assignment, the Scheduler checks the caregiver's credential, license or certification status and expiration date in the personnel record (PER-01) and confirms it meets the client's staffing requirement. The Scheduler does not assign a caregiver whose certification is expired, suspended or unverified.

If a client needs medication administered under the plan, only a CMT may administer. If the CMT is unavailable, the Scheduler notifies the Supervising RN immediately. The RN arranges a qualified substitute or other safe arrangements, and no one else administers the medication (SVC-06).

For Medicaid participants, the Scheduler also confirms that the worker has passed the criminal history records check and other pre-referral screening (PER-02), and that the worker is not the participant's representative.

Participants who direct their own services may choose their worker, but the choice must still meet the credential requirements above. The RN explains the credential requirements to the participant and documents the discussion (CR-09).

If a client's condition changes so that a non-certified aide is no longer appropriate, the RN reassesses within the timeframe in SVC-03, revises the determination, and tells the Scheduler. The Scheduler replaces the aide with a certified caregiver at the earliest possible time, and the RN arranges temporary measures to keep the client safe.
If a client revokes a waiver of skilled services, the Scheduler assigns a certified caregiver as soon as one is available, and the RN documents the revocation and the interim safety plan.

The Administrator reviews assignments monthly against the credential requirements and reports exceptions to the QA program (GOV-04). Any assignment that did not meet the requirement is treated as an incident under SAF-02.

responsibilities.duty: Determines and documents the certification requirement for each client, obtains waivers under CR-07, and reviews the determination at each supervisory visit and reassessment.
Assigns only caregivers who meet the requirement and have verified credentials, and notifies the RN when a qualified caregiver is unavailable.
Audits assignments, ensures credentials are verified, and addresses non-compliance.
Takes part in the risk and benefit discussion and signs the waiver if they choose a non-certified aide.

documentation: Caregiver Qualification Determination by the RN
Signed and dated waiver of skilled services, with a copy in the client record
Written staffing requirement in the scheduling system
Credential and certification verification for each assigned caregiver
Monthly assignment audit
Incident report for any non-compliant assignment

policies.title: Medication Assistance and Self-Administration Support
policies.applies_to: Supervising RN, CMTs, CNAs, non-certified aides, schedulers; all clients who need help with medications
policies.purpose: To ensure medications are administered only by qualified staff on physician orders, that clients who self-administer receive only the help permitted with informed consent, and that medications, errors and adverse reactions are documented and acted on.
policies.policy: Administration of drugs is governed by this written policy. Where agency staff administer medications, they must be licensed or certified, and under CFC a worker who administers medication must be a CMT. Medications are given only as ordered by the physician, and the client record documents each medication administered or taken, every medication error, and every adverse drug reaction, with the corrective action taken. A client who signs informed consent may receive assistance from a non-licensed individual with self-administration of medication. When staff only assist with self-administration, the RN supervisory visit is required at least every 3 months. When staff administer, it is required at least every 45 days. Aides do not administer, adjust or set up medications beyond what the plan of care and the RN's delegation allow. A client's representative may give consent only within the authority granted.

definitions.definition: Giving a medication to a client by a licensed or certified person (such as a CMT under RN delegation) on a physician's order.
Limited help given to a client who directs and takes their own medications, such as reminders or handing the client a container the client has prepared, as defined in the plan of care.
Any deviation from the physician's order, including a wrong drug, dose, time, route, client, or omitted dose.
An unexpected or harmful response to a medication.
Certified Medication Technician.

procedures: At the initial assessment and each reassessment, the Supervising RN reviews the client's medications, any physician orders and the client's ability to self-administer. The RN decides whether the client self-administers, needs assistance with self-administration, or needs staff to administer, and records the decision in the plan of care.

If staff are to administer medication, the RN obtains the physician's written or verbal order and records the medication, dose, route, time and purpose. The agency does not administer any medication without a physician's order. A current medication list is kept in the client record and updated at every change.

Only a CMT who holds current certification and has been delegated by the RN for that client may administer medication (SVC-04, SVC-05). The Scheduler confirms CMT status before each assignment. A CNA or non-certified aide may not administer medication.

If staff will assist with self-administration, the RN first holds an informed consent discussion with the client or representative, covering the help to be given, the risks and benefits, and the client's right to decline. The client or authorized representative signs and dates the consent, a copy is given to the client, and a copy is filed in the record (CR-07).

If the client has a representative, the RN confirms from the authorizing document that the representative's authority covers medical decisions before accepting consent from the representative. The agency does not honor a representative who exceeds the authority granted (CR-08). The participant's representative is not assigned as the worker.

The RN writes specific medication instructions for the caregiver: what the caregiver may do (for example remind the client, hand over the client's own container, observe) and what the caregiver may not do (for example set up, adjust or change doses). The caregiver signs that the instructions were received.

The CMT documents each administration on the Medication Administration Record at the time of administration: medication, dose, route, time, and initials. Each dose refused or omitted is recorded with the reason. For self-administration support, the caregiver records the help given and whether the client took the medication.

A caregiver who sees that medication is missing, expired, labeled differently from the order, or mixed up with another person's, does not give or assist with it, and calls the Supervising RN or the on-call number (SVC-11) immediately.

A caregiver who makes or finds a medication error calls the RN or on-call nurse immediately, ensures the client is safe, and calls 911 if the client is in danger. The RN contacts the physician for direction, and the caregiver does not give a corrective dose without instruction. The RN documents the error, notification, client response and corrective action in the record.

For an adverse drug reaction, the caregiver follows the emergency steps in SVC-10 and calls 911 if needed, then notifies the RN. The RN notifies the physician, documents the reaction and the actions taken, and updates the plan.

The RN reports medication errors and adverse reactions through the incident process (SAF-02). For Medicaid participants, incidents are reported within 24 hours of knowledge, with the written report within 7 calendar days on the Department's form, per REC-02.

At each supervisory visit, the RN reviews the medication record for accuracy and completeness, observes the caregiver's practice, and documents the findings. The RN makes visits at least every 45 days where staff administer and at least every 3 months where staff assist with self-administration, or sooner if the client's condition requires.
The RN retrains or removes from medication duties any caregiver whose practice does not meet the standard, and reports conduct that may be grounds for Board of Nursing action under PER-10.
The Administrator reviews all medication errors and reactions quarterly for patterns and reports to the QA program (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Decides the medication support level, obtains orders and consents, delegates to CMTs, supervises on schedule, and investigates errors and reactions.
Administers only ordered medications as delegated, documents each administration, and reports errors and reactions immediately.
Gives only the assistance with self-administration allowed in the plan, never administers, and reports concerns to the RN.
Assigns only a CMT where medication administration is required.
Ensures incident reporting and QA review of medication events.

documentation: Current medication list and physician orders
Informed consent for assistance with self-administration, signed and dated
Representative's authorization, if applicable
RN delegation record and written medication instructions
Medication Administration Record or self-administration assistance log
Medication error and adverse drug reaction reports with corrective action
Supervisory visit records reviewing medication practice

policies.title: Scheduling, Missed Visits and Continuity of Care
policies.applies_to: All schedulers, coordinators, RN supervisors, on-call staff and caregivers serving Medicaid (CFC/CPAS) and private-pay clients of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure every client receives the authorized services on schedule, that missed visits are found and corrected quickly, that clients keep control over who works with them and when, and that no Medicaid participant's services are interrupted, reduced or ended without proper authorization.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] schedules caregivers only within the hours authorized in the participant's plan of service and delivers services consistent with that plan. Participants direct their own services, including selecting, training, scheduling, setting duties for and dismissing their worker. The agency keeps a backup caregiver available so service continues when a regular caregiver is absent or dismissed. The agency does not suspend, terminate, increase or reduce services to a Medicaid participant without Department authorization and consultation with the participant. A participant's representative is never assigned as the participant's worker. Every missed visit is documented, the client is told, and repeated misses are reported to the RN and the supports planner. The 24/7 on-call line is always available so clients can report a missed visit at any time.

definitions.definition: The Department-authorized document listing the personal assistance services and hours a Medicaid participant is approved to receive. The agency bills only for services preauthorized in this plan.
A scheduled visit that does not occur, or that is not started within [30] minutes of the scheduled start time without the client's agreement to the change.
Two or more missed visits for the same client within any 30-day period, or any pattern the RN or Administrator judges to put the client's health or safety at risk.
One aide serving two participants during the same time under the shared-attendant service codes (W5521 for CFC, W5528 for CPAS), paid at a lower per-unit rate than single-participant service.
A qualified, screened and oriented caregiver who can cover a scheduled visit when the regular caregiver is unavailable or has been dismissed by the participant.
The person legally authorized or designated to act for the participant. A representative may not be assigned as the worker for that participant.

procedures: At intake, the Scheduler obtains the authorized plan of service for each Medicaid participant and enters the authorized hours and days into the scheduling system. Schedules may not exceed those hours.
The Scheduler confirms with each participant or representative the preferred days, start times, and the caregiver(s) the participant has chosen, and records these preferences in the client record.

Before assigning any caregiver, the Scheduler confirms that the caregiver meets the qualifications required for the tasks in the plan of service (see SVC-05) and that the caregiver is not the participant's representative. If the proposed caregiver is the representative, the assignment is refused and the Administrator is notified.

When two participants will share one aide, the Scheduler confirms that both participants have agreed in writing, that both plans of service allow shared service, and that the visit is set up and billed with the shared-attendant codes (W5521 or W5528). Shared-attendant service is billed at the lower shared rate ($4.2597 per 15-minute unit under the FY 2025 transmittal; the Billing Specialist confirms the current fee schedule each July).

The Scheduler identifies at least one backup caregiver for each client and lists the backup in the scheduling record. The backup is introduced to the client when practicable, and the client may accept or reject the backup without retaliation.
The Scheduler publishes the weekly schedule to caregivers and gives each client or representative the name of the scheduled caregiver and the 24/7 on-call number [PHONE].

A caregiver who cannot work a scheduled visit must notify the Scheduler or the on-call line as soon as the absence is known and, whenever possible, at least [4] hours before the visit. The caregiver may not arrange swaps directly with the client.

When a visit is at risk of being missed, the Scheduler or on-call staff assigns the backup caregiver or another qualified caregiver, and contacts the client to confirm the new arrival time. If no replacement can arrive within [1] hour of the scheduled time, the Scheduler calls the client or representative to explain and offer options.

The Scheduler reviews the electronic visit verification record daily (see SVC-08) to identify visits with no clock-in. Any visit without a clock-in within [30] minutes of the scheduled start is treated as a possible missed visit, and the Scheduler calls the caregiver and the client.
Each missed visit is entered in the Missed Visit Log with the date, client, caregiver, reason, who was notified, and the make-up or replacement action. The client is told the same day.
Clients may report a missed visit at any time through the 24/7 on-call line. On-call staff log the report, arrange coverage and notify the Scheduler the next business day (see SVC-11).

If a participant dismisses a worker or asks for a different schedule, the Scheduler honors the request within authorized hours, assigns a replacement the participant accepts, and documents the change. The dismissal is not treated as grounds to reduce or end services.

The Scheduler notifies the RN Supervisor and the participant's supports planner or case manager of repeated missed visits within [2] business days of the second miss, and records the notification. The RN decides whether the client's health or safety is at risk and whether a care plan review is needed.
The Administrator reviews the Missed Visit Log monthly for trends by caregiver, client and cause, and reports results to the quality assurance committee (see GOV-04).

Staff may not suspend, terminate, increase or reduce a Medicaid participant's services on their own. A request for any such change goes to the Administrator, who consults the participant and obtains Department authorization before action is taken (see SVC-12).

If a client has a missed visit and the agency cannot cover it, staff tell the client how to reach the on-call line and, if the client is at risk, the RN Supervisor arranges welfare contact or emergency response (see SVC-10).

responsibilities.duty: Approves staffing levels and backup coverage, reviews the Missed Visit Log monthly, and authorizes any change in service only after Department authorization and participant consultation.
Builds schedules within authorized hours, assigns qualified caregivers and backups, monitors visit verification, arranges coverage, logs missed visits and sends required notices.
Evaluates client risk after repeated missed visits, adjusts the plan of care or caregiver assignment as needed, and coordinates with the supports planner.
Reports to scheduled visits on time, notifies the agency promptly of any absence or delay, and does not leave a client without coverage or accept changes to hours directly.
Receives missed-visit reports at any hour, arranges coverage, and records the call in the on-call log.

documentation: Plan of service and authorized hours on file for each Medicaid participant
Client schedule preferences and chosen caregivers
Weekly schedule and backup caregiver list
Missed Visit Log with reason, notifications and coverage
Notices to the RN and supports planner about repeated missed visits
Shared-attendant consent and shared-visit records
Monthly missed-visit trend review

policies.title: Electronic Visit Verification (ISAS) and Timekeeping
policies.applies_to: All caregivers, schedulers, billing staff and administrators of [AGENCY NAME] who record or bill personal assistance time for Medicaid participants
policies.purpose: To make sure all Medicaid personal assistance time is documented through the Department-approved telephonic timekeeping system (ISAS), so that claims are accurate, supported and timely, and the agency meets the federal electronic visit verification requirement.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] and its workers use the Department-approved telephonic timekeeping system, ISAS, to document time and submit claims for Community First Choice and CPAS personal assistance. Caregivers call in at the start and out at the end of every shift. Visits are verified from the participant's primary landline or an approved OTP device. A caregiver's own phone number never matches the client's. Caregivers do not have ISAS portal access. The agency limits portal roles to authorized staff. Missing-time requests are used only for genuine system failures and are completed within the deadlines set by the Department. Claims are submitted within 12 months of the date of service, and sooner whenever practicable.

definitions.definition: The Department-approved telephonic timekeeping and claims system used for Medicaid personal assistance in Maryland. It documents time worked and generates claims. Maryland uses it to meet the federal EVV requirement.
A one-time password device supplied in place of a landline, used to verify that a visit took place at the participant's home.
The participant's registered home telephone number from which clock-in and clock-out calls are verified.

A request, with a stated reason, to add time that was worked but not captured by ISAS. Per 2020 ISAS training, requests are limited and due within 2 business days after month-end. The agency confirms current rules with the ISAS Help Desk.
ISAS portal user roles assigned to agency staff. The agency may hold up to 5 admin and 5 billing roles.

procedures: The Administrator designates in writing which staff hold ISAS admin and billing roles (no more than 5 of each) and records each person's name, role and date assigned. Roles are removed on the day a person leaves or changes duties.

During onboarding of each Medicaid participant, the Billing Specialist confirms that the participant's primary landline or OTP device is registered in ISAS and records the number or device ID in the client record.

The Billing Specialist confirms that no caregiver's registered telephone number matches the client's number. If a match is found, the caregiver may not be scheduled for that client until the conflict is resolved and the Administrator is informed.

During orientation (see PER-03), each caregiver is trained to use the ISAS telephone process, including the call-in and call-out steps, the dialing sequence, what to do if the line is busy or out of service, and how to identify the client being served. The caregiver signs a training acknowledgment.

Caregivers call ISAS from the client's verified landline or OTP device at the start of each shift, before beginning any task, and call again at the end of the shift, after the last task is done. Caregivers may not clock in early, clock out late, or clock in from another location.
Caregivers do not log into the ISAS portal and do not receive portal credentials. Corrections and requests go through the Scheduler or Billing Specialist.

Caregivers who cannot complete a call because of a phone or system problem notify the Scheduler or on-call line immediately, and write the actual start and end times on the visit note before leaving the home.

The Scheduler reviews ISAS data daily for visits with no clock-in, no clock-out, short or long visits, or visits that do not match the schedule, and contacts the caregiver and client the same day to learn what happened (see SVC-07).

The Billing Specialist reviews time against the plan of service each week. The agency does not bill hours that exceed those authorized. Where the system reduces hours above the plan of service automatically, the Billing Specialist records the reason.

The Billing Specialist tracks the number of missing-time requests used for each month and for each participant. Missing-time requests are used only when time was actually worked, the reason is documented, and a supervisor has verified it with the client and caregiver.

Missing-time requests are submitted by the deadline in the Department's current rules. Based on 2020 ISAS training, the agency treats this as 2 business days after the end of the month, and confirms the current rules with the ISAS Help Desk (1-855-463-5877) each January and whenever the Department announces changes.
Time is reconciled by the Thursday–Wednesday ISAS workweek where relevant, and the Billing Specialist confirms that payroll hours and ISAS hours are consistent before payroll is closed (see PER-06).
The Billing Specialist reconciles ISAS time to the monthly participant signature log and the plan of service before releasing any claim (see SVC-09).
Claims generated through ISAS are reviewed and submitted no later than [30] days after the date of service. In no case may a claim be submitted more than 12 months after the date of service.

Any suspected falsification, such as clocking in from the wrong phone, having another person clock in, or billing time not worked, is reported to the Administrator and investigated under GOV-05. Confirmed problems result in discipline, correction of claims and, where required, repayment.
The Administrator reviews an ISAS exception report each month (missing time used, visits with no clock-in, phone mismatches) and reports trends to the quality assurance committee.

responsibilities.duty: Assigns and removes ISAS admin and billing roles, reviews monthly exception reports, and ensures timekeeping complies with Department requirements.
Registers participant phone numbers/OTP devices, reconciles ISAS to the plan of service and signature logs, manages missing-time requests, and submits claims on time.
Reviews visit verification daily, follows up on missing calls, and prevents phone-number conflicts.
Calls ISAS at the start and end of every shift from the client's verified phone, never from a number that matches the client's, and reports system problems immediately.

documentation: ISAS role assignment record (admin and billing)
Participant landline/OTP registration record
Caregiver ISAS training acknowledgment
Daily visit-verification review notes
Missing-time request log with reasons, approvals and dates submitted
Reconciliation of ISAS time to plan of service and signature log
Claim submission dates
Monthly ISAS exception report

policies.title: Monthly Participant Signature, Eligibility Verification and Service Documentation
policies.applies_to: All billing staff, coordinators, RN supervisors and caregivers of [AGENCY NAME] who deliver, document or bill Medicaid personal assistance
policies.purpose: To make sure that Medicaid personal assistance services are verified by the participant, billed only for eligible participants, supported by retained records, and delivered by qualified workers.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] collects and keeps the participant's (or representative's) signature verifying the services provided at least monthly. The agency verifies each participant's Medicaid eligibility at the start of each month of service. Documentation of the dates and hours of service is kept for 6 years from the date of service in a manner approved by the Department. ISAS time is reconciled to the monthly signature log and the plan of service before any claim is billed. The agency obtains written verification of the qualifications of every worker and provides a copy of the worker's license or credentials on request.

definitions.definition: The signature, at least once a month, of the participant or the participant's representative verifying the services the worker provided in that month.
A check, performed at the beginning of each month of service, that the participant is enrolled in and eligible for Maryland Medicaid for that month.
Records showing the dates and hours of service, including visit verification data, caregiver notes and signature logs.
Written evidence that a worker meets the requirements for the services provided, such as certification, license, criminal history check results and training.

procedures: On the first business day of each month, the Billing Specialist checks each Medicaid participant's eligibility for that month through the Department's eligibility verification system and prints or saves the result with the date, time and name of the verifier.

If a participant is not eligible or eligibility cannot be confirmed, the Billing Specialist informs the Administrator and the RN Supervisor the same day. The agency does not bill for any period for which eligibility is not confirmed. The Administrator contacts the participant and the supports planner, and no service is stopped without following SVC-12.
The Scheduler gives each participant or representative a monthly signature form listing the dates, caregiver names and hours worked, drawn from ISAS data, at least once each month.

The participant or representative reviews the form, corrects any errors in writing, and signs and dates it. The caregiver does not sign for the participant. A caregiver who is also the participant's representative is not permitted, because a representative may not be assigned as the worker.

If a participant cannot sign (for example, due to hospitalization or physical limitation), the representative signs and notes the reason. If neither can sign, the RN Supervisor documents the reason and attempts to get a signature within [10] business days.

The Billing Specialist tracks signature collection and follows up with the participant, representative or caregiver by the [10th] day of the following month on any missing signatures. The Administrator is told of any signature not received by the [15th].

Before billing, the Billing Specialist reconciles three sources for each participant and month: ISAS time, the signed monthly log, and the authorized hours in the plan of service. Differences are resolved and documented before the claim is released.
Claims are not released for any month where the signature is missing without the Administrator's written approval and a documented reason. The agency does not create, alter or back-date a signature.
Visit notes and timekeeping records are stored in the client record in the system approved by the Department, with each entry showing the date, start and end times, caregiver and tasks performed.

Documentation of dates and hours of service is retained for 6 years from the date of service. The Administrator ensures records are not destroyed before then, even if the client has been discharged (see REC-01).

Before a worker is assigned, the Personnel Coordinator obtains and files written verification of the worker's qualifications, including certification or license status, criminal history record check result, training, and any required health screening (see PER-01, PER-02, PER-03, PER-04).
When a participant, the supports planner or the Department asks for a worker's credentials, the Personnel Coordinator provides a copy of the license or certificate within [2] business days.
The Billing Specialist reports to the Administrator each month on eligibility checks done, signatures collected, claims held, and exceptions found.
The Administrator samples at least [10] percent of claims each quarter against the signature log, ISAS data and plan of service, and reports results to the quality assurance committee (see GOV-04).
Errors found after billing, such as a claim for an ineligible month or hours not supported by records, are corrected and any overpayment is reported and repaid in accordance with SVC-14 and GOV-05.

responsibilities.duty: Verifies eligibility monthly, tracks signatures, reconciles ISAS to the signature log and plan of service, and holds claims that are not supported.
Produces monthly signature forms and assists with collection.
Reviews cases where the participant cannot sign and ensures the signature process does not interfere with services.
Obtains and keeps written verification of each worker's qualifications and supplies credentials on request.
Approves exceptions, audits claims quarterly and ensures records are retained for 6 years.

documentation: Monthly eligibility verification record (date, time, verifier)
Monthly signed participant/representative verification form
ISAS time reports and reconciliation worksheet
Visit notes
Signature follow-up log and exception approvals
Worker qualification verification file
Quarterly claim audit results

policies.title: Change in Client Condition and Emergencies in the Home
policies.applies_to: All caregivers, RN supervisors, on-call staff and administrators of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure that caregivers recognize and report changes in a client's condition and emergencies promptly, that the RN assesses significant changes within required timeframes, and that incidents are reported to the right parties on time.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] trains every caregiver to identify situations that need RN referral, including a significant change in a client's condition. Caregivers report such changes to the RN or on-call staff at once. The RN assesses a client who has had a significant change in condition within 48 hours, or within 7 calendar days if the RN documents that a 48-hour assessment is not necessary. Caregivers call 911 for any life-threatening emergency and then call the agency. Incidents and complaints are reported within 24 hours of the agency's knowledge, with a written report within 7 calendar days on the Department's form. Suspected abuse, neglect, self-neglect or exploitation is reported immediately to the local department of social services.

definitions.definition: A change in a client's physical, mental or functional status that is new, sudden, or beyond what is expected, such as a fall, new confusion, new pain, change in skin, breathing, eating or drinking, a hospital or ER visit, or a change in the client's ability to do daily activities. The RN decides whether a change is significant.
A situation in which delay in medical care could cause death or serious harm, such as unresponsiveness, chest pain, trouble breathing, stroke signs, severe bleeding, choking or a serious fall.
An event involving a client or caregiver that affects or could affect health, safety or rights, including injury, death, abuse, neglect, exploitation, theft, medication error, or a missing client.
The 24-hour, 7-day telephone line staffed by agency personnel able to respond to clinical and scheduling concerns (see SVC-11).

procedures: During orientation, the RN trains each caregiver using a checklist of changes that require RN referral. Training includes supervised practice, return demonstration and a signed acknowledgment (see PER-03). Training is repeated at least annually.

Each caregiver receives a wallet card or app note with the on-call number [PHONE], the RN Supervisor's contact, and the 911 instruction. The on-call number is also posted in the client's home copy of the care plan.

If a client is in a life-threatening emergency, the caregiver calls 911 first, stays with the client, gives basic first aid or CPR within the scope of training, and then calls the on-call line as soon as the client is safe.

The caregiver does not move an injured client except to prevent further harm, does not give medication or treatment outside the plan of care, and does not transport the client in the caregiver's own vehicle unless allowed under SAF-06.

For a change in condition that is not a 911 emergency, the caregiver calls the on-call line immediately and does not wait for the end of the shift. The caregiver describes what was seen, when it started and what the client or representative says.

On-call staff record the call, ask the clinical questions on the call script, and refer the caregiver to the RN. The RN, or a designated licensed nurse, decides whether the client needs 911, urgent care, a physician or nurse practitioner call, or other action, consistent with medical and nursing standards.

The RN notifies the client's representative and, as the plan of care and the client's wishes allow, the physician or nurse practitioner, and the supports planner or case manager for Medicaid participants.

The RN assesses the client within 48 hours of learning of a significant change in condition. If the RN determines that a 48-hour assessment is unnecessary, the RN writes the reason in the record and completes the assessment within 7 calendar days.
After assessment, the RN updates the plan of care and worker instructions, and informs the caregiver and Scheduler of any changes in services or precautions (see SVC-03).

If the client is taken to the hospital, the caregiver reports to the on-call line, gives emergency responders the client's medication list and contacts as available, and does not leave the client alone if still on duty unless authorized.

Any incident, including injury, death, medication error, theft, abuse allegation or missing client, is reported to the Administrator or on-call administrator right away and no later than the end of the shift.

The Administrator reports incidents and complaints to the Department within 24 hours of the agency's knowledge and files the written report on the Department's form within 7 calendar days (see SAF-02, REC-02).

For suspected abuse, neglect, self-neglect or exploitation, the Administrator or RN notifies the local department of social services immediately (see SAF-01). This is done by phone and is not delayed for internal review.

The RN documents the change in condition, assessment, actions and notifications in the client record on the same day, and the caregiver documents what was seen and done in the visit note before leaving the home.
The Administrator reviews every emergency and significant change at the next quality assurance review to find trends and training needs (see GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Recognizes and reports changes in condition immediately, calls 911 for life-threatening emergencies, stays with the client within scope, and documents what was seen and done.
Trains caregivers, directs the response to reports, assesses the client within 48 hours (or 7 days when documented), and updates the plan of care.
Answers calls, logs them, routes them to the RN or an administrator and responds within 1 hour.
Files incident reports within 24 hours and 7 calendar days, notifies the local department of social services of suspected abuse or neglect, and reviews events for trends.

documentation: Caregiver training checklist and acknowledgment on change-in-condition recognition
On-call log entry
Visit note and incident report
RN assessment within 48 hours, or documentation of why 7 calendar days was used
Updated plan of care and worker instructions
Notifications to representative, physician/NP and supports planner
Department incident report submitted within 7 calendar days and proof of 24-hour report
Local department of social services report record

policies.title: 24/7 On-Call Services
policies.applies_to: All on-call staff, RN supervisors, administrators and caregivers of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure that clients, representatives and caregivers can reach a responsible agency representative at any time, and that emergency inquiries receive a timely response consistent with medical and nursing standards.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains a 24-hour, 7-day on-call service. Clients or their representatives can reach an agency representative by communication device at any hour. Emergency inquiries are recognized and routed to an individual who can respond consistent with medical and nursing standards. The agency responds no later than 1 hour after it receives an inquiry, or sooner if medical standards require. Every inquiry is recorded in an on-call log showing the identity of the responding personnel, the content of the inquiry and the time of the inquiry. Written on-call procedures and the on-call phone number are given to every client.

definitions.definition: The after-hours and around-the-clock service that lets clients, representatives and caregivers reach a live agency representative.
A call describing a possible emergency or urgent change in a client's condition, a missed visit that puts a client at risk, an injury, or any situation needing prompt nursing judgment.
The record of each inquiry that shows who responded, the content of the inquiry, and the time received and the time of the response.
The written instructions given to clients explaining how to reach the agency after hours and what to expect.

procedures: The Administrator assigns an on-call schedule at least [2] weeks ahead, listing on-call staff and a backup. Each on-call staff member has a licensed nurse or the RN Supervisor available for clinical consultation at all times.

The Administrator keeps one published on-call number, [PHONE], that rings to the on-call staff member's communication device at all times. The number is tested at least weekly, and a test record is kept.

Before starting services, the Intake Coordinator gives each client or representative a copy of the written on-call procedures with the on-call phone number, explains how to use it, and records the date in the client record. The same number appears on the client's service agreement and care plan.

Each caregiver receives the on-call number and the written on-call procedures during orientation, and is told to call for any change in a client's condition, missed visit concerns, safety problems, and any emergency inquiry from the client.
On-call staff answer all calls live. If a call cannot be answered, the call is forwarded to the backup within [5] minutes. Voicemail alone does not meet this policy.

On-call staff recognize emergency inquiries using the agency's call script. Anything involving a possible life-threatening condition is handled immediately: the caller is told to call 911 if not already done, and the on-call nurse is notified at once.

Emergency inquiries are routed to a licensed nurse or other individual who can respond consistent with medical and nursing standards. That individual responds to the caller no later than 1 hour after the agency receives the call, and sooner if medical standards require.

Non-emergency inquiries, such as scheduling changes or caregiver lateness, are handled by on-call staff, who arrange coverage using the backup caregiver list (see SVC-07) and are also answered within 1 hour.

For every inquiry, the on-call staff member immediately records in the on-call log: the date and time received, the caller and client names, the content of the inquiry, the name of the person who responded, the time of the response and the action taken.

If a call raises a significant change in condition, an incident, or suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation, on-call staff start SVC-10 and SAF-01 steps and notify the RN Supervisor and Administrator.
The next business day, on-call staff give the RN Supervisor and Scheduler a summary of calls so that follow-up care, visits, plan updates and documentation in the client record can be completed.
The RN Supervisor reviews the on-call log weekly to check response times and that every inquiry was answered and closed. Any inquiry not answered within 1 hour is reviewed as a quality issue.
The Administrator reviews the on-call log monthly, reports response-time performance and trends to the quality assurance committee (see GOV-04), and fixes coverage gaps.
On-call staff are trained during orientation and annually in the call script, triage, emergency recognition, confidentiality and documentation, and sign a record of training (see PER-03).
The Administrator keeps on-call logs and schedules as part of agency records and makes them available to surveyors on request (see REC-03).

responsibilities.duty: Maintains the on-call schedule and phone, reviews the log monthly and ensures 24/7 coverage.
Answers calls, applies the call script, routes emergencies to a nurse, ensures a response within 1 hour, and completes the log.
Provides clinical direction, responds to emergency inquiries, and reviews the on-call log weekly.
Gives written on-call procedures and the phone number to each client or representative at start of service.
Uses the on-call line for emergencies, changes in condition and scheduling problems.

documentation: On-call schedule and weekly phone test record
On-call log (identity of responder, content and time of each inquiry)
Written on-call procedures with proof of delivery to each client
On-call training records
Weekly RN review and monthly Administrator review notes
Follow-up summaries to RN Supervisor and Scheduler

policies.title: Discharge, Transfer, Suspension and Discontinuation of Services
policies.applies_to: All administrators, RN supervisors, coordinators and billing staff of [AGENCY NAME] involved in ending, suspending, reducing or transferring client services
policies.purpose: To make sure that services are discharged, transferred, suspended or discontinued safely and lawfully, that Medicaid participants keep their services until the Department authorizes any change, and that records and notices are handled properly.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] does not suspend, terminate, increase or reduce services for a Medicaid participant without Department authorization and consultation with the participant or representative. When services are suspended or terminated, the agency submits a transition plan to the case manager or supports planner and the participant. Discharged-client records are completed within 30 days of discharge and kept for 5 years after discharge, or 6 years from the date of service for Medicaid service documentation, whichever is longer. The agency gives the Department 45 days' written notice of closure, sale or similar events, with a transition plan. A client may refuse or withdraw from treatment at any time, and the agency explains the associated risks and honors the decision.

definitions.definition: The end of all services to a client by [AGENCY NAME].
A temporary stop of services, for example during a hospital stay or when services cannot safely be provided.

A written plan describing how the participant's care will continue after services end or are suspended, including the receiving provider where known, the date of transfer, medication and care information to be shared, and risks.
The person who coordinates the participant's Medicaid long-term services and supports and is responsible for the plan of service.
A client's or representative's decision to refuse or stop some or all services.

procedures: Any staff member who believes services should be stopped, suspended, reduced or increased reports to the RN Supervisor and Administrator. Staff may not tell a client that services will end or change until the Administrator has approved the process in this policy.

For a Medicaid participant, the Administrator first consults with the participant or representative about the reason and the options, including whether the concern can be solved with a different caregiver, a revised schedule or other support.

The Administrator then requests Department authorization for any suspension, termination, increase or reduction, and sends the request to the supports planner or case manager in writing with the reason and the date of the consultation. Services continue as authorized until the Department approves the change.

If the participant's health or safety is in immediate danger or the caregiver's safety is at risk, the Administrator takes protective action, such as emergency response, reassigning the caregiver or calling for adult protective services (see SAF-01 and SAF-05), and notifies the supports planner immediately. Any further change still follows Department authorization.

When services are to be suspended or terminated, the RN Supervisor prepares a transition plan within [5] business days and sends it to the case manager or supports planner and to the participant or representative. The plan covers continued care needs, medications, equipment, contacts and any receiving agency.

For a private-pay client, the Administrator gives written notice of discharge at least [14] calendar days ahead (agency standard), except where there is an immediate safety risk, nonpayment after notice, or the client asks to end services sooner. The notice gives the reason and the transition plan.

Clients may refuse treatment or services, or withdraw from them, at any time. The RN Supervisor explains the risks of refusing or withdrawing, documents the discussion, obtains the client's signed refusal or waiver where applicable, and revises the plan of care (see CR-07).

If a client chooses to end services, the Administrator confirms the choice in writing, notifies the supports planner for Medicaid participants, gives the client contact information for other providers on request, and completes a discharge summary.

Before a discharge date, the RN Supervisor reviews the client record, completes a discharge summary with the reason, condition at discharge and referrals, and sends relevant information to the receiving provider with the client's written consent.

The Scheduler removes the client from the schedule on the discharge date and informs caregivers. The Billing Specialist closes billing, reconciles ISAS time and the final monthly signature (see SVC-09) and returns any client-owned property or documents.

The Records Clerk completes and closes the discharged client's record within 30 days of discharge, checks that every note, signature and assessment is present, and locks the record against unauthorized changes.

Client records are kept for 5 years after discharge, and until age 21 or 5 years after the record was made, whichever is later, for minors. Documentation of dates and hours of Medicaid service is kept 6 years from the date of service. Records are stored with safeguards against loss, destruction and unauthorized use, and are released only as allowed under CR-03 and REC-01.

If the agency plans to close, sell, change ownership, location, name or tax ID, the Administrator gives MDH 45 days' written notice that includes how participants will be told and a transition plan (see GOV-06). Participants and supports planners are notified in writing in time to arrange other services.
On closure, client records are returned to the client or representative or retained as required by law, and the Administrator documents where records are held and how they may be requested.
The Administrator reviews every discharge, suspension and transfer at the next quality assurance meeting to look for patterns in reasons and any missed notices (see GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Consults the participant, obtains Department authorization, issues notices, gives 45-day notice to MDH for closure or similar events, and ensures records are retained.
Explains risks of refusal or withdrawal, prepares transition plans and discharge summaries, and coordinates handoff of care.
Removes discharged clients from the schedule and informs caregivers on the discharge date.
Closes billing and reconciles final time and signatures.
Completes and secures the discharged record within 30 days and tracks retention dates.

documentation: Record of consultation with the participant or representative
Department authorization request and response
Transition plan and proof it was sent to the supports planner and participant
Written discharge notice (private-pay) or client's withdrawal/refusal documentation
Risk discussion and signed refusal or waiver
Discharge summary
Record completion date (within 30 days) and retention schedule
45-day notice to MDH and participant notices on closure or sale

policies.title: Coordination with Medicaid Programs, Supports Planners and Payers
policies.applies_to: Administrator, Supervising RN, intake and scheduling staff, billing staff, and caregivers serving Medicaid participants
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] delivers services consistent with each Medicaid participant's plan of service and works with the supports planner, the nurse monitor, the Department and other payers. Services are then authorized, coordinated and communicated clearly to the client.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] participates in Community First Choice (COMAR 10.09.84) and CPAS (COMAR 10.09.20) as a licensed Residential Service Agency that employs a Registered Nurse. We serve only participants whose plan of service names [AGENCY NAME] as their chosen personal assistance agency. We coordinate with the participant's supports planner and nurse monitor and share participant information only on the Department's forms and through its procedures. We do not suspend, terminate, increase or reduce services without Department authorization and consultation with the participant. For clients covered by managed-care benefit plans or other third-party payors, we keep records as the payor requires. Within the agency and with other providers, we state who is responsible for each part of care and tell the client in writing.

definitions.definition: The Department-authorized document that lists the personal assistance services a participant is approved for and names the participant's chosen agency.
The person who develops and manages the participant's plan of service and who receives transition and change information from the agency.
The nurse monitoring provider designated by the Department for the participant. [AGENCY NAME]'s RN coordinates with this person but does not replace this role.
Any managed-care organization, insurer or other entity that pays for or authorizes a client's services other than the client.

procedures: At referral, intake staff confirm the participant's program (CFC or CPAS), their Medicaid eligibility, and that the plan of service or referral names [AGENCY NAME] as the chosen agency. Intake staff document this in the intake record (see SVC-02).
Intake staff record the supports planner's name, phone and email and the nurse monitor's name and contact in the client record before services start.
Before the first visit, billing staff confirm the authorized services, hours and dates on the plan of service. Scheduling staff build the schedule only for authorized services (see SVC-07).

The Supervising RN reviews the plan of service when completing the agency assessment and plan of care (see SVC-03). The RN confirms that agency tasks match the authorized services and notes any mismatch for the supports planner.
The Supervising RN contacts the participant's nurse monitor, as needed, to coordinate on clinical concerns. The RN records the date, person contacted and outcome in the client record.

Staff share participant information with the supports planner, nurse monitor, Department or payor only on the Department's forms and procedures, or as the payor requires. Staff check the minimum-necessary standard in CR-03 before sending anything.

If a participant needs more or fewer hours, a change in service, or a new service, the Supervising RN notifies the supports planner within one business day. Staff continue to bill and provide only the authorized services until the Department authorizes the change.

Staff never suspend, terminate, increase or reduce services on their own initiative. For any proposed discontinuation, the Administrator consults the participant, requests Department authorization, and sends a written transition plan to the supports planner and participant (see SVC-12).

When a significant change in condition or emergency occurs, the Supervising RN tells the supports planner, and the nurse monitor when appropriate, as soon as practicable. Documentation follows SVC-10.

For clients on managed-care plans or other payors, billing staff request each payor's authorization and records requirements before services start. They keep the records in the form and for the time period the payor requires.

The Supervising RN gives each client a written summary of who coordinates the client's care. It lists caregiver name, RN supervisor, 24/7 number, supports planner, nurse monitor, and any other provider involved, and says who is responsible for each part of care. The client or representative acknowledges receipt, and a copy goes in the record.
When another provider shares in a client's care, the RN documents each provider's responsibilities. The RN shares the care plan with that provider with the client's consent.

When a client asks about community resources or emergency response equipment, staff refer them to Maryland Access Point at 1-844-MAP-LINK, or to the Office of Long Term Services and Supports (OLTSS) at 410-767-1739.
The Administrator directs RSA program or compliance questions to mdh.cfcprovidersrsas@maryland.gov and logs the question, date and answer.
Billing staff verify the participant's Medicaid eligibility at the start of each month of service (see SVC-09).
The Administrator reviews a sample of coordination records quarterly as part of quality assurance (see GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Maintains program participation, ensures staff follow Department procedures, and approves any request to change or end services.
Coordinates clinically with the supports planner and nurse monitor, documents contacts, and ensures the plan of care matches the plan of service.
Verify the plan of service and contact information, schedule only authorized services, and report changes to the RN.
Confirm authorizations and eligibility, and keep payor records as required.
Deliver only services in the plan and report changes or needs to the Supervising RN.

documentation: Intake record showing program, eligibility, plan of service and contact details
Log of contacts with the supports planner, nurse monitor and payors
Written care coordination summary with client acknowledgment
Authorization records and payor-required records
Compliance question log for mdh.cfcprovidersrsas@maryland.gov

policies.title: Medicaid Billing, Rates, Claims and Overpayment Recovery
policies.applies_to: Administrator, billing staff, schedulers, Supervising RN and caregivers who use ISAS
policies.purpose: To ensure [AGENCY NAME] bills Medicaid only for authorized services that were actually delivered and documented. It also ensures claims are timely and accurate at the correct rate, and overpayments are found and refunded promptly.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] bills only for personal assistance that is preauthorized in the plan of service, delivered consistent with it, and within our provider agreement. Time is documented and claims are generated through the Department-approved telephonic timekeeping system (ISAS). We submit claims within the billing time limit. The CFC Billing Manual states 12 months from the date of service, and the Medicaid regulation COMAR 10.09.36.06 sets the regulatory limit, so we follow the stricter.
