policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
policies.applies_to: All employees, independent contractors, contractual employees, and subcontracted caregivers
policies.purpose: To set clear standards of ethical conduct and professional boundaries that protect clients, preserve trust, prevent exploitation and conflicts of interest, and meet Maryland training and Medicaid participation requirements.
policies.policy: All staff must act ethically, respect client confidentiality and dignity, and keep professional boundaries with clients and families. Ethics and confidentiality are part of required training (COMAR 10.07.05.11). [AGENCY NAME] is free of conflicts of interest as Medicaid participation requires (COMAR 10.09.84.05). A participant's representative may not be assigned as that participant's caregiver (COMAR 10.09.84.06). Caregivers accept instruction on the plan of service from the participant or representative, the nurse monitor, a treating physician or nurse practitioner, or MDH, and not from other persons. Violations lead to corrective action up to termination and, where required, reports to the Board of Nursing, OHCQ, and the local department of social services.

definitions.definition: The limit that separates a worker's professional role from personal or social involvement with a client or the client's family.
A relationship with a client beyond the caregiver role, such as business, financial, romantic, or close social relationships, or serving as the client's legal agent.
A situation in which a staff member's or the agency's personal, financial or other interest could influence, or appear to influence, client care, service decisions or billing.
Money, goods, services, loans, or favors given to or by staff or a client.

procedures: At hire and annually, every staff member receives this policy and signs an acknowledgment, which is filed in the personnel file (see PER-05).

Orientation and annual training include ethical behavior, confidentiality, professional boundaries, prevention of abuse and neglect, and recognizing situations that need RN referral. Each session is documented in the personnel file (see PER-03).

Gifts: Staff may not ask for or accept money, gift cards, loans, personal property, or other gifts from clients or their families. A staff member offered a gift politely declines and reports the offer to the supervisor the same day. If refusal would harm the relationship, the supervisor may approve acceptance of a token item of nominal value, and the approval is documented (see CR-04).

Staff may not borrow from, lend money to, sell to, buy from, or enter into business or financial dealings with a client. Staff may not use client funds, cards, accounts or property for personal purposes, and may not be named in a client's will or as beneficiary without Administrator review and documentation.

Personal relationships: Staff may not enter into romantic or sexual relationships with clients, and may not seek social or personal friendship with clients outside the care role. Staff may not use the client's home, phone or vehicle for personal reasons.

Dual relationships: A staff member who has a pre-existing personal relationship with a client or family member discloses it to the Director of Nursing before any assignment. The Director of Nursing decides on the assignment and records the decision.

Representatives: The scheduler may not assign a participant's representative as that participant's worker. The RN checks the representative's name against the proposed worker before each new assignment and documents the check on the assignment record (see CR-08 and SVC-05).

Instruction on the plan of service: Caregivers follow the plan of service and accept instruction about it only from the participant or representative, the nurse monitor, a treating physician or nurse practitioner, or MDH. Any instruction outside the plan, or from any other person, is not followed. The caregiver reports it to the RN the same day (see SVC-01).

Social media and electronic communication: Staff may not post client names, photos, addresses, health information or visit details on social media or in personal messaging, and may not take photos or videos of clients unless the plan of service and a written client consent allow it. Staff may not accept or send friend or follow requests with clients or their families during the period of service. Staff communicate with clients using agency-approved means (see CR-03).
Confidentiality: Staff discuss client information only with those who need it for care. Breaches are reported to the Administrator the same day, who follows the privacy breach process (see CR-03).

Conflicts of interest: Staff and principals disclose any financial interest in a vendor, referral source or client that could affect agency decisions or Medicaid billing. The Administrator reviews each disclosure within 10 business days, documents the outcome and, where appropriate, removes the person from related decisions (see GOV-05).

Staff may not recruit clients for outside employment, solicit private-pay arrangements, or provide paid services to agency clients outside the agency, and may not accept payment directly from a client for services within the plan of service.

A staff member who observes or suspects a violation reports it to the Director of Nursing or Administrator immediately. Suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation is also reported under SAF-01. Retaliation against anyone who reports in good faith is prohibited.

The Director of Nursing or Administrator investigates each report within 5 business days, records findings, and applies corrective action under the agency's disciplinary process. A staff member may be removed from client assignments during the investigation.
Conduct that may be grounds for Board of Nursing action is reported immediately to the Board of Nursing and OHCQ under PER-10.
The Administrator reviews boundary violations and trends annually with the QA committee (see GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Enforces this policy, reviews conflict-of-interest disclosures, and decides on discipline and external reports.
Reviews dual relationships and representative conflicts before assignments, trains staff, and investigates reports.
Does not assign a representative as the participant's worker or any conflicted caregiver.
Follow the plan of service, decline gifts, keep boundaries and confidentiality, and report violations.

policies.title: Worker Classification Certification (Health-General §19-4A-11) and Annual PCA Wage Report
policies.applies_to: Administrator, the person who controls pay and employment practices, payroll staff
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] meets the RSA worker-classification certification required for obtaining and keeping its license under Health-General §19-4A-11 and files the annual personal care aide wage report with the Department of Labor on time.
policies.policy: The person who controls [AGENCY NAME]'s pay and employment practices must read the RSA-PCA Guidance Document and submit the online RSA Certification form to OHCQ. This is a condition of both obtaining and keeping the license. Aides are classified as W-2 employees unless counsel advises otherwise in writing. [AGENCY NAME] files the annual RSA personal care aide wage report, with the average, highest and lowest PCA wage rates, with the Department of Labor by September 1 each year under HB 189/SB 371 of 2024.

definitions.definition: The online form on the OHCQ Residential Service Agencies page that the person controlling pay and employment practices submits after reading the RSA-PCA Guidance Document.

definitions.term: Person who controls pay and employment practices
definitions.definition: The owner, officer or other individual with authority over how workers are paid and classified, identified in the agency's records as [NAME AND TITLE].
The yearly report to the Maryland Department of Labor of the average, highest and lowest wage rates paid to personal care aides.
A worker the agency treats as an employee for tax and wage purposes, with withholding and employer-paid payroll taxes.

procedures: The Administrator identifies in writing the person who controls pay and employment practices ([NAME AND TITLE]) and records the designation in the compliance file. If control changes, the Administrator updates the designation within 5 business days.

Before the license application is submitted, the designated person reads the full RSA-PCA Guidance Document, obtained from the OHCQ Residential Service Agencies page, and signs and dates a reading acknowledgment kept in the compliance file.
The designated person submits the online RSA Certification form on the OHCQ RSA page and saves the confirmation (screenshot, email or confirmation number) in the compliance file.

The Administrator treats the certification as a condition of licensure. Before the license is considered complete or renewed, the Administrator confirms the certification is on file and current. At each renewal (see GOV-02), the designated person re-reads the Guidance Document and confirms with OHCQ whether a new submission is needed.

If the person who controls pay or employment practices changes, or the agency's classification practices change materially, the designated person re-reads the Guidance Document and contacts OHCQ to confirm whether a new submission is required, and the outcome is documented.
Aides are hired and paid as W-2 employees, with withholding and employer taxes, and are subject to the wage and leave rules of PER-06.

Any proposal to classify any aide as an independent contractor requires written advice from counsel, Administrator approval and a documented review under the FLSA and State law. Without that written advice, no aide is paid as an independent contractor. The decision is kept in the compliance file.

By July 15 each year, the Payroll Lead pulls the pay rates of all personal care aides for the reporting period from the payroll system and calculates the average, highest and lowest wage rates, using the format and period specified by the Department of Labor.

The Payroll Lead documents the calculation method, the data source and the number of aides included, and a second person (the Administrator or a designee) verifies the figures against payroll records by August 1.
The Administrator or Payroll Lead files the report with the Department of Labor by September 1 through the method the Department prescribes, and saves proof of submission.
If the Department of Labor changes the form, method or due date, the Payroll Lead updates this procedure within 30 days of learning of the change.
If a filing is missed or found to be wrong, the Administrator files the report or a correction immediately, documents the reason and corrective action, and informs the QA committee.
The Administrator checks the status of the certification and the wage report at each annual compliance review and reports results to the QA committee (see GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Designates the responsible person, verifies certification and report filing, and approves any classification change.

responsibilities.duty: Reads the Guidance Document, submits the online certification, and keeps it current.
Prepares and files the annual PCA wage report and keeps supporting data.
Advises in writing on any non-W-2 classification.

Signed acknowledgment of reading the RSA-PCA Guidance Document
RSA Certification form confirmation

policies.title: Job Descriptions, Qualifications and Skill Assessments
policies.applies_to: Administrator, Director of Nursing/RN, scheduler/ISAS billing coordinator, aides (CNA, CMT, non-certified), and all other employees and contractors
policies.purpose: To make sure every position at [AGENCY NAME] has a written job description with minimum education and qualifications, and that every employee and contractor has a documented skills assessment before client assignment, as COMAR 10.07.05.08 and 10.07.05.10 require.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains a written job description with educational and other qualifications for every employee and contractor position, and performs a documented skill assessment of every employee and contractor. Job descriptions are written for the Director/Administrator, the Registered Nurse, the Scheduler/ISAS Billing Coordinator, and aides (CNA, CMT and non-certified). The RN position must be filled by an employee when the agency serves Community First Choice and CPAS participants. COMAR 10.07.05 sets no administrator credential, so the agency sets the Administrator's minimum qualifications in the job description. Workers who administer medications must be CMTs, and workers who perform other delegated nursing functions must also be CNAs. Criminal history checks are required for all direct service workers, including nurses.

definitions.definition: A written statement of a position's title, reporting line, duties, required education, licensure or certification, experience, and physical and other requirements.
A documented evaluation of a person's ability to perform the tasks of the job, including a skills demonstration, completed before the person is assigned to clients.
Certified Nursing Assistant, certified in Maryland and able to receive delegated nursing tasks under COMAR 10.27.11.
Certified Medication Technician, certified to administer medications.
A caregiver who is not a CNA or CMT, who may be assigned only under the conditions in SVC-05 and COMAR 10.07.05.10.

procedures: The Administrator approves a written job description for each position before it is advertised or filled: Director/Administrator, Registered Nurse, Scheduler/ISAS Billing Coordinator, CNA, CMT, and non-certified aide. Each shows title, supervisor, duties, education, licensure or certification, and experience.

Director/Administrator description: The agency sets in writing the minimum education and experience, including management experience in home care or health services, as [ADMINISTRATOR QUALIFICATIONS]. The description includes responsibility for compliance, QA, staffing, records and reports to OHCQ and MDH, and notes that COMAR 10.07.05 sets no administrator credential.

RN description: Requires a current Maryland RN license (or compact privilege as allowed) in good standing, and [YEARS] of clinical experience. Duties include assessing each new participant, developing the plan of care or plan of service and worker instructions, assigning staff, delegating nursing tasks to CNAs or CMTs under COMAR 10.27.11, supervising and instructing workers, and monitoring clients. The RN is an employee of [AGENCY NAME] when serving CFC/CPAS participants.

Scheduler/ISAS Billing Coordinator description: Duties include scheduling, matching workers and clients, EVV/ISAS monitoring, preparing claims from ISAS, verifying monthly Medicaid eligibility, and billing only preauthorized services. Required education is [EDUCATION] and experience is [EXPERIENCE].

CNA description: Requires current Maryland CNA certification in good standing. Duties include personal care, delegated nursing tasks as instructed by the RN, and documentation. CMT description: Requires current CMT certification, in addition to CNA certification where the worker performs other delegated nursing functions, and covers medication administration under RN delegation (see SVC-06).

Non-certified aide description: Requires completion of the training in PER-03 and limits assignments to clients who need no ADL help, who need ADL help with no predictable adverse health consequences in the supervising nurse's judgment, or who have signed a waiver of skilled services (see CR-07 and SVC-05). A non-certified aide may not administer medications.
Each description states the criminal history check, licensure or certification verification, health screening including TB, and training requirements of the position (see PER-01 to PER-04).

Before the first client assignment, the RN performs a skill assessment of every employee and contractor using the agency's Skills Assessment Checklist, which covers personal care tasks, standard precautions, safe transfers, recognition of changes in condition, documentation, and tasks specific to the role, and includes an in-person demonstration.

The RN records on the checklist the date, observed skills, pass or needs training result, and signs it. A person who does not pass receives supervised practice and training and is reassessed. No unassessed person is assigned to a client.

The RN repeats skill assessments at least annually and whenever a worker is assigned to a client with new or complex care needs, a task is delegated, or a performance concern arises. Each result is filed in the personnel file (see PER-05).

Contractors and subcontracted caregivers meet the same job description, qualifications and skill assessment standards. The agency obtains written evidence of the subcontractor's verification (see GOV-09).

At hire, each employee receives and signs the job description for their position, and the signed copy is filed in the personnel file. The Administrator reviews all job descriptions at least annually and when duties, regulations or program requirements change (see GOV-03).
The Custodian audits files quarterly to confirm that each worker has a current job description, qualifications on file and a skill assessment (see PER-05).

responsibilities.duty: Approves job descriptions, sets the Administrator's qualifications, hires only qualified applicants, and reviews descriptions annually.
Performs and signs skill assessments, ensures worker qualifications fit the client's needs, and delegates only to qualified CNAs and CMTs.
Assigns only workers whose files show a current job description, qualifications and skill assessment.
Files job descriptions and assessments and tracks annual reassessment due dates.

policies.title: Reporting Caregiver Misconduct to the Board of Nursing and OHCQ
policies.applies_to: Administrator, Director of Nursing/RN, supervisors, and all staff who become aware of caregiver misconduct
policies.purpose: To make sure that [AGENCY NAME] immediately reports to the Maryland Board of Nursing and OHCQ any action or inaction by a referred individual that may be grounds for action under the Health Occupations Article, as COMAR 10.07.05.10 requires.
policies.policy: If [AGENCY NAME] becomes aware of an action or inaction by a referred individual that may be grounds for action under the Health Occupations Article, including §8-316 and §8-6A-10, it reports it immediately to the Board of Nursing and OHCQ. The agency does not wait for the end of its own investigation before reporting. Nursing administrators, RNs, LPNs and CNAs who report have immunity under Courts and Judicial Proceedings §5-709, and other persons have immunity under §5-708. Staff are protected from retaliation for reporting. The agency documents each report and the date it was submitted.

definitions.definition: Any employee, independent contractor or contractual employee referred or assigned by the agency to provide care to a client.
As soon as the agency is aware of the conduct, and no later than the end of the same business day, unless a documented emergency prevents it. In that case, the report is made as soon as possible.

definitions.term: Misconduct that may be grounds for Board action
definitions.definition: Conduct by a nurse or nursing assistant that may be a basis for discipline under the Health Occupations Article, such as client abuse or neglect, theft or financial exploitation, diversion of drugs, practice outside scope, practicing while impaired, falsifying records, or practicing without a valid license or certification.
The Maryland Board of Nursing, which licenses and certifies nurses and nursing assistants.

procedures: Any staff member who sees or learns of conduct or inaction by a referred individual that may be grounds for Board action tells the Director of Nursing or Administrator at once, by phone or in person, and no later than the end of the shift.

The Director of Nursing or Administrator immediately takes steps to protect clients, which may include removing the individual from client assignments and arranging a replacement. If a client is in danger, call 911 first (see SVC-10).

The Administrator decides, without delay and on the day of notice, whether the conduct may be grounds for Board action. When in doubt, the agency reports, and it does not hold the report for a decision by counsel or further investigation.

If the conduct involves suspected abuse, neglect, self-neglect or exploitation of a client, the agency also notifies the local department of social services immediately, in line with SAF-01. If a reportable incident has occurred, the agency also follows incident reporting timelines (SAF-02).

The Administrator or Director of Nursing reports the conduct to the Board of Nursing at [BOARD OF NURSING CONTACT AND REPORTING METHOD], using the Board's complaint or reporting process, and to OHCQ at 410-402-8040 or on the OHCQ complaint line at 800-492-6005, followed by written confirmation if first reported by phone.

The report includes the name and license or certification number of the individual, the date, time and place of the conduct, a factual description, the client's initials or identifier (without unnecessary protected information), witness names, actions taken by the agency, and the name and phone of the person making the report.
Reports contain facts only, with no speculation. The agency shares only information needed for the report and follows HIPAA when disclosing client information (see CR-03).

The agency does not require the individual's consent for the report, and does not threaten, discourage or retaliate against any person who makes a report in good faith. A report cannot be withheld because the individual resigns or is terminated.

The Administrator records the report on the Board/OHCQ Misconduct Report Log, including the date and time of the report, the person who made it, the agencies notified, the method used, the confirmation or reference number, and the actions taken.

The agency keeps a copy of the written report and any acknowledgment in a confidential compliance file, separate from the individual's routine personnel file, with a cross-reference noted in the personnel file (see PER-05).
The agency cooperates fully with Board and OHCQ requests for information, and the Administrator is the point of contact. Records are produced promptly (see REC-03).
The agency completes its own internal investigation within 14 days, records the findings and corrective action, and sends updated information to the Board and OHCQ if it affects the earlier report.

The agency does not rehire or reassign the individual to client care while a Board action is pending unless the Director of Nursing and Administrator document that clients are protected, and the agency verifies the individual's license or certification status first (see PER-01).

Annually, staff are trained on this policy, including who has reporting immunity under Courts and Judicial Proceedings §5-709 (nursing administrators, RNs, LPNs and CNAs) and §5-708 (others), and that staff are protected for reporting. Training is documented (see PER-03).
The Administrator reviews the log at least quarterly to confirm every case was reported on time and reports results to the QA committee (see GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Makes the decision to report, ensures reports are made immediately to the Board of Nursing and OHCQ, and keeps the log.
Removes the individual from care if needed, assists with the report, and investigates clinical aspects.
Report suspected misconduct at once and cooperate in investigations.
Maintains the confidential report file and checks license status.

documentation: Board/OHCQ Misconduct Report Log with dates and times of submission
Copies of written reports and acknowledgments
Notes of telephone reports

policies.title: Client Records, Clinical Records and Retention
policies.applies_to: Administrator, RN Supervisor, office and records staff, schedulers, and all caregivers who create or handle client records
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] keeps a complete, accurate, confidential and retrievable record for every client, keeps each record for the full required period, and protects records from loss, destruction and unauthorized use.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains a record for every client who receives services. The record contains the RN assessments, plans of care and plans of service, RN supervisory visit documentation, informed consent and waiver forms, medication documentation, client representative documentation, and Medicaid service documentation showing dates and hours of service. Client records are kept for 5 years after discharge. For a minor, the record is kept until the client reaches age 21 or for 5 years after the record is made, whichever is later. Medicaid service documentation (dates and hours) is kept for 6 years from the date of service. Where more than one period applies, [AGENCY NAME] keeps the record for the longer period. The record of a discharged client is completed within 30 days of discharge. Records are confidential and are released only with the client's written consent or as permitted by Maryland law on medical records. Records are safeguarded against loss, destruction and unauthorized use. If [AGENCY NAME] closes, records are returned to the client or representative or retained as required.

definitions.definition: The complete set of documents kept for one client, in paper or electronic form, covering intake, assessments, plans, consents, supervision, medications, communications, incidents, service documentation and discharge.
The date services to the client end for any reason, including client choice, transfer, loss of eligibility, or agency-initiated discontinuation.
Records showing the dates and hours of Medicaid-funded services delivered, including electronic visit verification data, caregiver timesheets and monthly participant signature records.
An instruction from the Administrator that a record must not be destroyed because of a pending audit, investigation, complaint, claim or litigation, even if the retention period has ended.

procedures: At intake, office staff open a record for each client using the agency's standard record checklist and assign a unique client record number. The record is created on the same day the service request is received.

The Administrator and RN Supervisor review the record checklist at least annually. They compare it with current OHCQ requirements for clinical record content and with Medicaid program requirements, and they update it if requirements change.

The RN Supervisor places in the record the RN assessment, the plan of care (and the Medicaid plan of service where applicable), and each reassessment. This is done within 2 business days of the date each document is completed.

The RN Supervisor places in the record the documentation of each on-site supervisory visit, including the date, findings, and any changes made to the plan or caregiver assignment. Documentation is completed within 2 business days of the visit.

Office staff file each signed and dated informed consent and each waiver of skilled services in the record. The record also holds the RN's note of the risk and benefit discussion. A copy of each form is given to the client or representative.

Caregivers and the RN document medication assistance or administration as required by SVC-06. Documentation includes medications given or assisted, medication errors and adverse reactions, and it is filed in the record. Medication orders from the physician are filed when medications are administered.
Office staff file client representative documentation in the record, including the representative's name, authority, contact information and any advance directive provided by the client (see CR-08).

Schedulers and billing staff keep service documentation for each date of service, including electronic visit verification data, caregiver documentation and monthly participant signatures. This documentation is retained for at least 6 years from the date of service.

Every entry in a record is dated and attributable to the person who made it. Corrections to paper records are made by a single line through the error, with the date and initials of the person correcting it. Electronic systems must keep an audit trail. Entries must never be erased or backdated.

Staff may access a client record only to the extent needed to do their jobs. Paper records are stored in locked cabinets in the agency's business office. Electronic records are stored in systems that require individual log-ins, are backed up at least daily, and are accessible only to authorized staff.

Records are released only with the client's or representative's signed written consent, or as permitted by Maryland law on medical records and by HIPAA (see CR-03). Staff log every release in the record, with the date, recipient, items released and staff member. Requests the staff member cannot decide go to the Administrator.

Within 30 days after a client is discharged, the RN Supervisor and office staff complete the record. They add the discharge summary, the final service documentation, and any outstanding signatures, notes and notices. The Administrator signs off that the record is complete.

Office staff mark the retention-end date on each discharged record. The date is the later of 5 years after discharge and 6 years after the last date of service, or, for a minor, the later of age 21 and 5 years after the record is made, if that is longer than the other periods.

Before any record is destroyed, the Administrator confirms in writing that the retention period has ended and that no legal hold, audit, investigation, complaint or claim is pending. Records are then destroyed by shredding or secure electronic deletion, and the destruction is entered in the records destruction log.
If a legal hold applies, the Administrator notifies records staff in writing, and the affected records are tagged and kept until the Administrator releases the hold in writing.

If a record is lost, stolen or accessed without authorization, the person who discovers it notifies the Administrator immediately. The Administrator investigates, documents the response, and applies the breach assessment and notification steps in CR-03 and the incident reporting steps in SAF-02.

If [AGENCY NAME] plans to close, the Administrator follows GOV-06. Records are returned to the client or representative, or retained as required, and a retention plan identifies where and by whom the records will be kept, with how to request them. The Administrator documents the plan, and the notice to clients includes contact information for obtaining records: [PHONE] and [ADDRESS].

The RN Supervisor audits a sample of active records and of recently discharged records at least quarterly for completeness, timeliness and legibility, and reports the findings to the Administrator under GOV-04. Missing items are corrected within 14 calendar days.

responsibilities.duty: Owns this policy. Approves record destruction, issues and releases legal holds, approves the record checklist, and ensures safeguards and retention are in place.

Ensures clinical documents (assessments, plans, supervisory visits, consents, medication documentation) are complete and filed on time, completes discharge records, and conducts the quarterly record audit.
Create and file records, control access and releases, log releases, manage storage and backups, track retention dates, and carry out approved destruction.
Document services accurately and on time, return paperwork to the office as instructed, and never share or remove client records except as directed.

documentation: Client record (paper or electronic) with record checklist
Record release log
Retention schedule and record destruction log
Legal hold notices
Discharge record completion sign-off (within 30 days of discharge)
Quarterly record audit reports
Closure records retention plan, if applicable

policies.title: Required Reports to the State
policies.applies_to: Administrator, RN Supervisor, compliance and billing staff, office staff, and any staff who learn of a reportable event
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] submits every report, survey, notice and filing required by Maryland licensing and Medicaid rules on time, to the correct agency, with a record of when and how it was submitted.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] reports incidents and complaints within 24 hours of learning of them, followed by a written report within 7 calendar days on the Department's form. [AGENCY NAME] notifies the local department of social services immediately of suspected abuse, neglect, self-neglect or exploitation. [AGENCY NAME] reports immediately to the Board of Nursing and to OHCQ any conduct that may be grounds for Board of Nursing action. [AGENCY NAME] also completes the annual data collection survey with each license renewal, files the annual HCBS Cost Survey, files the annual personal care aide wage report with the Maryland Department of Labor by September 1, gives MDH 45 days' notice of closure, sale, ownership, location, name or tax ID changes, and submits plans of correction within 15 calendar days of an audit finding. The Administrator keeps a regulatory reporting calendar and a log of every report filed.

definitions.definition: An event involving a client, caregiver or the agency that must be reported to the state under SAF-02, including injuries, deaths, abuse, neglect, exploitation, and serious complaints.
The time at which any [AGENCY NAME] employee or contractor first learns of an incident or complaint. The 24-hour period starts at that point, not when a supervisor is informed.

The annual home and community-based services cost survey required by the Maryland Department of Health. For FY 2026 it is due December 31, 2026, and payment is suspended starting January 1, 2027 for providers that do not file.
The annual report on personal care aide wages that RSAs file with the Maryland Department of Labor by September 1 (HB 189/SB 371 of 2024).
A written plan submitted to the agency that cited a finding, stating how and when each deficiency will be fixed.

procedures: The Administrator keeps a regulatory reporting calendar listing every recurring report, its due date, the responsible person and the agency it goes to. The calendar is reviewed at the monthly management meeting, and reminders are set at 60 and 30 days before each due date.

Any employee or contractor who learns of an incident or complaint reports it to the RN Supervisor or Administrator immediately, and in no case later than the end of the shift. The Administrator or designee records the date and time of first knowledge.

For a reportable incident or complaint, the Administrator or designee files the report with the Department within 24 hours of first knowledge. The designee documents the date, time, method and the person who submitted it.

The RN Supervisor or Administrator completes the written incident or complaint report on the Department's form and submits it within 7 calendar days of first knowledge. The report is filed in the incident file and, where relevant, in the client record.

For suspected abuse, neglect, self-neglect or exploitation of a client, the person who has the suspicion contacts the local department of social services at [LOCAL DSS PHONE] immediately, without waiting for the Administrator. The Administrator then confirms the report was made, documents it, and follows SAF-01.

If a caregiver's conduct may be grounds for Board of Nursing action, the Administrator reports it immediately to the Board of Nursing and to OHCQ (410-402-8040) as set out in PER-10. The report and the confirmation of submission are kept in the personnel file and in the compliance file.

If a client or other person complains to OHCQ, or if OHCQ requests a complaint investigation report, the Administrator provides the report immediately as set out in CR-02 and REC-03. Complaint investigation reports are written as required in CR-02.

The Administrator submits the annual data collection survey whenever OHCQ requires it. The survey is also included with each license renewal application, which is filed before the license expires with the $1,000 fee and the other renewal items listed in GOV-02. The Administrator signs the survey.

The Administrator and billing staff complete and submit the annual HCBS Cost Survey on the Department's schedule and confirm that it has been accepted. For FY 2026 the survey is due December 31, 2026. Missing the deadline suspends payment beginning January 1, 2027, so the internal deadline is November 30.

The Administrator and payroll staff prepare and file the annual personal care aide wage report with the Maryland Department of Labor by September 1 of each year. Payroll staff pull the underlying wage data from payroll records by July 15 and the Administrator reviews and signs it before filing. The filing confirmation is kept in the compliance file.

The Administrator follows the 80% direct-care compensation standard and the rate transparency requirements in the federal access rule (42 CFR 441.302(k) and 447.203), which apply from July 9, 2030 according to MDH's 2024 report. The Administrator reviews MDH guidance each year and has payroll and billing report the direct-care share of Medicaid payments to the governing body as part of GOV-04.

For closure, sale, change of ownership, location, name or tax ID, the Administrator gives MDH written notice at least 45 days beforehand, following GOV-06. The notice is dated, sent by a method that provides proof of delivery, and kept in the compliance file.

When the agency receives audit findings or a statement of deficiencies, the Administrator prepares a plan of correction and submits it within 15 calendar days of the finding. The plan states each correction, the person responsible and the completion date. Follow-up and evidence of correction are documented under GOV-08.

If the agency learns that any information it provided in a license application or renewal has changed, such as owner information, prior license actions, criminal charges, or Medicare or Medicaid violations, the Administrator reports the change to OHCQ promptly, as set out in GOV-02.

Subcontracted agencies must give [AGENCY NAME] evidence that they have verified personnel information as required by state rules. The Administrator collects this evidence on the schedule in the subcontract and keeps it in the compliance file (see GOV-09).
The Administrator keeps a log of every report filed with date, time, agency, method, who filed it and confirmation. Copies of all reports and confirmations are kept for at least 6 years.

Each quarter, the Administrator reviews the log against the reporting calendar to confirm that nothing is overdue. Late or missed reports are reviewed as a quality event under GOV-04, and corrective steps are documented.

responsibilities.duty: Owns the reporting calendar and makes or approves all state filings, signs the surveys and wage report, and files plans of correction on time.
Receives clinical incident information, prepares written incident reports within 7 calendar days, and supports reports of caregiver conduct to the Board of Nursing.
Gather data for the HCBS Cost Survey and the personal care aide wage report on the internal deadlines, and keep the supporting records.
Report any incident, complaint or suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation immediately, and contact the local department of social services right away if they suspect abuse, neglect or exploitation.

documentation: Regulatory reporting calendar
Log of reports filed, with confirmations
Incident and complaint reports (24-hour reports and 7-day written reports on the Department's form)
Records of notices to the local department of social services
Reports to the Board of Nursing and OHCQ about caregiver conduct
Data collection survey and renewal filings
HCBS Cost Survey submission and acceptance
Annual personal care aide wage report and filing confirmation
45-day notices to MDH
Plans of correction and evidence of completion

policies.title: Regulatory Inspections, Surveys and Records Access
policies.applies_to: Administrator, RN Supervisor, office staff, and all employees who may be present when a surveyor, auditor or other government representative arrives
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] cooperates fully and professionally with inspections, surveys, reviews and audits by authorized government agents, and that required records are organized, protected and available promptly.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] cooperates with all required inspections, reviews and audits by authorized government agents, including OHCQ and Maryland Medicaid. OHCQ may inspect before it approves or denies a license, and each additional pre-licensure visit caused by noncompliance may cost $250. [AGENCY NAME] makes complaint investigation reports available to OHCQ immediately on request. The Administrator designates staff to receive surveyors, and personnel and client records are kept available in the agency's business office. Employees do not hide, alter, back-date or destroy records, and they do not retaliate against any person who speaks with a surveyor.

definitions.definition: Any authorized government representative who conducts an inspection, survey, review or audit of [AGENCY NAME], including OHCQ staff, Medicaid program and compliance staff, and their agents.
An inspection OHCQ may conduct before it approves or denies a license application. Each additional visit required because of noncompliance may be charged at $250.
The agency's licensed business location at [ADDRESS], where personnel and screening records and client records are kept and available for review.

procedures: The Administrator designates, in writing, a primary and a backup person to receive surveyors ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME] and the RN Supervisor, unless otherwise named). The names and phone numbers are posted at the reception area and given to all office staff.

Any employee who is approached by a person claiming to be a surveyor greets them courteously, asks for identification and the purpose of the visit, and immediately contacts the primary designee. If the primary designee is unavailable, the employee contacts the backup. Surveyors are not left unattended in the lobby for longer than necessary.

The designee verifies the surveyor's identification and authority, records the name, agency, time of arrival and purpose of the visit in the survey log, and notifies the Administrator, who attends as soon as possible.

The Administrator keeps the following available at the business office during business hours: the license, the policy and procedure manual, personnel files including screening and training records, client records, complaint records and investigation reports, incident reports, billing and service documentation, on-call procedures and the call log, and subcontract agreements and subcontractor verification evidence.

The designee provides the records the surveyor asks for promptly. Requests for complaint investigation reports are met immediately. The designee keeps a list of every record reviewed, copied or removed, and makes a copy of anything the surveyor takes.

The designee gives the surveyor a work space and escorts the surveyor to areas where records are kept. Records may be reviewed only by authorized surveyors, and the designee does not let anyone else view client records during the visit.

If the surveyor wants to visit a client at home or speak with a client, the designee asks the client or representative first and respects the client's decision. Staff do not coach clients or caregivers on what to say, and the client's services are not disrupted.

Employees answer surveyors' questions truthfully and within their job duties. If an employee does not know an answer, the employee says so and refers the question to the designee. Employees may ask to have the Administrator or RN Supervisor present.

No one may alter, back-date, remove, conceal or destroy any record in anticipation of or during a survey. Any late documentation must be dated with the actual date it was written and labeled as late entry. Violations lead to discipline under PER-07, up to termination.
No employee, client or contractor may be retaliated against or discouraged from speaking with a surveyor or filing a complaint. The Administrator reminds staff of this at orientation and annually.
The designee takes notes during the visit, including what was asked, what was provided and what the surveyor mentioned as concerns. The notes are kept in the survey file.

At the exit conference, the Administrator and RN Supervisor attend and listen to the surveyor's findings, ask for clarification, and write down each finding. If the surveyor gives a written statement of findings, the Administrator signs for receipt, not for agreement, unless the form says otherwise.

For any finding, the Administrator prepares a plan of correction and submits it within the time set by the agency that conducted the review. For Medicaid compliance audit findings the plan of correction is due within 15 calendar days, as set out in GOV-08 and REC-02. The Administrator assigns responsibility and completion dates and checks that each correction was done.

If OHCQ makes an additional pre-licensure visit because of noncompliance, the Administrator corrects the deficiency before the visit. The Administrator budgets for and pays the $250 charge per additional visit, and records the reason in the compliance file.

When OHCQ requests a complaint investigation report or asks for a public summary, the Administrator provides the report immediately and provides the summary as permitted by law, redacting confidential client information as required (see CR-02 and CR-03).
The Administrator reviews every survey, audit and inspection result with the governing body and the quality assurance committee under GOV-04, and tracks trends and repeat findings.

Each year the Administrator runs a mock inspection using the license requirements and the policy manual, checks that records are in order and available, and corrects any gaps within 30 days. The results are recorded in the compliance file.

responsibilities.duty: Designates and trains staff to receive surveyors, attends the entrance and exit conferences, makes sure records are available, and submits plans of correction on time.
Serves as backup designee, explains clinical practice and documentation to surveyors, and leads correction of clinical findings.
Greet surveyors, check identification, notify the designee right away, and keep personnel and client records filed and accessible in the business office.
Cooperate truthfully, never alter or hide records, and never retaliate against anyone who speaks with a surveyor.

documentation: Survey log (date, surveyor, agency, purpose)
List of records reviewed, copied or removed
Designee notes and exit conference notes
Statements of findings and plans of correction, with evidence of completion
Records of any additional pre-licensure visit charges
Annual mock inspection results
Written designation of survey contacts
